geometry_edits.rationale: Retarget the dominant massing toward a winged courtyard response so the frontage can become an active threshold without losing the protected primary mass ancestry.
Use a lateral split aligned to the building’s long axis to support a clearer court and side mass relation.
Open a more legible void between wings so the public center reads at massing scale.
Keep a connective upper link so the mass remains unified while the void becomes publicly meaningful.
Anchor the ground edge to preserve a continuous public threshold and prevent the split from becoming detached fragments.

graph_edits.rationale: Strengthen the program-required public void and convert the compact object into a clearer courtyard-bearing mass.
Increase courtyard depth so the void reads as usable public space rather than a minor subtraction.
Align the void with the verified access side to create a legible street threshold.
Lower and lengthen the terrace link so it reads as an inhabited public connector rather than a small appendage.

rationale: The candidate is coherent as a four-view mass and its overall diagonal/terraced gesture is readable, but it does not fully resolve the neighborhood-living brief. The volume sits within the parcel and responds to the site orientation, yet the access edge is not convincingly converted into a public threshold; the blue frontage reads as adjacent rather than actively engaged. The mass also trends toward a compact stepped object, with the section doing more silhouette work than program work. There is some courtyard/void implication, but it is not opened enough to count as a strong public ground figure. Compared with the supplied neighborhood references, it partially resonates with courtyards, bridges, and terraced sections, but it remains weaker in active ground logic and sectional program clarity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More sculptural and pavilion-like than the candidate; stronger courtyard legibility and lighter void treatment than this mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact multi-part mass organized around a clear central void with a lifted/bridged threshold and calm upper massing.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is much broader and more distributed than the candidate; do not copy the large campus scale.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A campus-like arrangement can still fit neighborhood living when the open center is the dominant organizer and the perimeter masses remain subordinate.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more compact and steeper; the reference’s transparency and lateral spread are not directly transferable.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Long horizontal massing with a carved central void and a roof that reads as one continuous section can support active mixed-use ground conditions.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate lacks the same clarity of walkable terrace sequence and reads more like a stacked object.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/ribbon-like sectioning can reinforce neighborhood-scale public circulation and turn section into usable outdoor room.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The candidate is more monolithic and less winged, so the courtyard effect is weaker.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking wings around a courtyard can preserve hierarchy while creating a legible public center and bridges/thresholds.

warnings: Access edge response is semantically weak: the verified frontage does not read as a clear entry seam, court, or undercut.
The form is coherent across views, but the void is underdeveloped and the ground plane feels too sealed.
Section reads as a stepped object more than an inhabited neighborhood threshold; program support is plausible but not yet convincing.
